01

Key findings

Interim report. The matrix covers ten business tasks across eight industries and ten departments, each run on three models and three effort levels (90 runs). 90 runs are complete so far — FS Account Plan, MFG Supply Risk, HLS Workforce, RET Campaign, PS Budget Review, ENU IT Dashboard, PRO Compliance, EXEC QBR, CS Themes, PMO Actions — and the findings below use only those. They will be refreshed as the remaining tasks are run.

Effort setting is the biggest cost lever.

Maximum effort costs 2–9× more than Light for the same task. Medium lands in between at 18–108% of Maximum — usually the right default.

The task drives cost more than the model.

At the same effort level, cost varies up to 13× between tasks but only 7× between models. Size the deliverable first: decks average 1,125 credits, documents 639, workbooks 577, dashboards 444.

No single model wins.

Auto is cheapest in 13 of 30 comparable cases, Opus 5 in 17. Picking the wrong one can cost up to 7× more for identical work.

Fable 5.1 is the premium option.

Never the cheapest in any of the 30 comparisons, and up to 7× the cost of Auto or Opus 5. Reserve it for work where the output quality justifies the premium.

Higher effort buys length, not compliance.

Every output met its structural brief at every effort level — all 26 decks hit the requested slide count and all 27 workbooks the required sheets. Extra effort mainly adds words and rows.

Decks don't link their sources.

Documents, workbooks and dashboards include clickable citations. All 27 decks name sources as plain text only — ask explicitly for a linked sources slide where auditability matters.

02

Test design

Ten realistic business tasks — one per department, spread across industries and output formats — each executed with the same prompt on every combination of model and effort level. Every prompt tells Cowork to use Work IQ (email, Teams, meetings, files) as the primary source, Web Search for public benchmarks, and to cite sources.

Factors

  • Task — 10 tasks: FS Account Plan, MFG Supply Risk, HLS Workforce, RET Campaign, PS Budget Review, ENU IT Dashboard, PRO Compliance, EXEC QBR, CS Themes, PMO Actions
  • Model — Auto Opus 5 Fable 5.1
  • Effort level — Light Medium Maximum
  • Output type (fixed per task) — DOCX 3 tasks · XLSX 3 tasks · PPTX 3 tasks · HTML 1 task

What is recorded per run

  • Cost in Copilot credits and the equivalent in USD, as entered in the workbook
  • Skills & plugins invoked and the tools Cowork called (Calendar, SharePoint, Microsoft Graph, Outlook, People, Teams, Web Search, Work IQ)
  • The generated artefact, kept in the SharePoint output_v2 folder and profiled below (words, slides, sheets, tables, charts, source links)

A run counts as complete when both the cost and the output file are available. Outputs whose cost is still to be entered are shown but excluded from every cost figure.

Prompts

FS Account Plan Financial Services (Banking) · Sales / Account Management · Word document · runs #1, #2, #3, #4, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9…
Build an account plan for my most active banking customer this quarter. Pull the latest context from my emails, Teams chats and meetings with that account, plus any related files in SharePoint/OneDrive. Then use Web Search for the customer's latest public news, results and strategic priorities. Produce a Word document with: executive summary, relationship map, open opportunities and risks, competitive landscape, and a 90-day action plan. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
MFG Supply Risk Manufacturing · Operations / Supply Chain · Excel workbook · runs #10, #11, #12, #13, #14, #15, #16, #17, …
Create a supply-chain risk tracker. Scan my email and Teams for supplier, logistics, delay or shortage discussions in the last 90 days, and check my meeting notes for related decisions. Use Web Search for current commodity price and freight trend indicators. Produce an Excel workbook with a Risk Register (risk, supplier, impact, likelihood, owner, mitigation, source) plus a Summary sheet with counts by severity. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
HLS Workforce Healthcare / Life Sciences · Human Resources · PowerPoint deck · runs #19, #20, #21, #22, #23, #24, #25, #26, …
Prepare a workforce and hiring update for leadership. Use my email, Teams and meetings to gather current hiring, onboarding and retention topics my team is discussing, and my org data for team structure. Use Web Search for current healthcare talent market and clinical staffing trends. Produce a 6-slide PowerPoint: current state, key issues, market context, risks, recommendations, next steps. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
RET Campaign Retail / Consumer Goods · Marketing · PowerPoint deck · runs #28, #29, #30, #31, #32, #33, #34, #35, …
Build a campaign readout deck. Pull campaign performance discussions, approvals and asset feedback from my email, Teams and recent meetings, plus any campaign files I have. Use Web Search for competitor campaigns and current retail consumer trends. Produce a 5-slide PowerPoint: results vs goals, what worked, competitive/market context, learnings, next campaign plan. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
PS Budget Review Public Sector / Government · Finance · Excel workbook · runs #37, #38, #39, #40, #41, #42, #43, #44, …
Produce a budget and spend review. Extract budget, cost, invoice and approval items from my email and Teams for the current fiscal period, and any budget spreadsheets I have. Use Web Search for public-sector inflation and procurement cost benchmarks. Produce an Excel workbook with a line-item sheet (item, owner, planned, actual, variance, comment) and a variance summary with totals. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
ENU IT Dashboard Energy & Utilities · IT / Engineering · HTML dashboard · runs #46, #47, #48, #49, #50, #51, #52, #53, …
Create a single-page HTML status dashboard for our current technology programme. Gather status, blockers, owners and milestones from my email, Teams channels and recent meeting transcripts. Use Web Search for relevant vendor roadmap or product release information. Produce a self-contained HTML page with programme health cards, milestone timeline, risk table and an external-signals section. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
PRO Compliance Professional Services · Legal / Compliance · Word document · runs #55, #56, #57, #58, #59, #60, #61, #62, …
Draft a compliance readiness brief. Search my email, Teams and files for policy, audit, privacy or regulatory discussions in the last 6 months. Use Web Search for the current status of the relevant regulations (e.g. EU AI Act, GDPR guidance) and recent enforcement examples. Produce a Word document with: scope, internal findings, regulatory landscape, gap analysis table, and prioritised remediation actions with owners. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
EXEC QBR Cross-industry · Executive Leadership · PowerPoint deck · runs #64, #65, #66, #67, #68, #69, #70, #71, …
Build a QBR deck for my business. Use my calendar, email, Teams and files from the last quarter to reconstruct what we delivered, what slipped and what decisions were made. Use Web Search for market and competitor developments in that period. Produce a 6-slide PowerPoint: quarter at a glance, delivery scorecard, market context, risks and issues, asks/decisions needed, next-quarter priorities. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
CS Themes Cross-industry · Customer Service / Support · Word document · runs #73, #74, #75, #76, #77, #78, #79, #80, …
Summarise customer support themes and produce an improvement plan. Mine my email and Teams for escalations, complaints and recurring issues in the last 90 days, plus meeting discussions about support quality. Use Web Search for current customer-service benchmarks (CSAT, first-contact resolution). Produce a Word document with: top themes with evidence, root causes, benchmark comparison table, and a prioritised improvement plan. Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.
PMO Actions Cross-industry · Project / Programme Management · Excel workbook · runs #82, #83, #84, #85, #86, #87, #88, #89, …
Create a consolidated action-item and RAID tracker. Pull open actions, owners and due dates from my recent meeting transcripts, Teams chats and email threads. Use Web Search only to validate any external dependency dates (vendor releases, regulatory deadlines). Produce an Excel workbook with an Actions sheet (action, owner, source, due date, status) and a RAID sheet (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies). Use my M365 Work IQ (email, Teams chats, meetings and files) as the primary source, and Web Search for external/public benchmarks. Cite sources.

07

Evidence

Every output file is paired with its run, grouped by task and ordered Auto → Opus 5 → Fable 5.1, Light → Medium → Maximum. Cards show the exact prompt that produced the run, page or slide previews rendered from the file, the output profile, and links to open, download or browse the original file in the public GitHub evidence folder. "Open in viewer" shows the real Office file in the Microsoft Office web viewer — no download or sign-in needed; HTML dashboards are embedded live. To place runs next to each other, use Compare runs side by side.

08

Recommendations

Interim working rules from the 90 complete runs. They are inferences from single runs on three tasks, not measured policy — see the caveats below.

Start at Medium; step down before stepping up.

Medium delivered complete, on-spec outputs at 18–108% of the Maximum cost, and every effort level met the structural asks (requested slide count, multi-sheet workbooks, cited Word documents). Light is usually cheaper again, but not always — in 6 pairs it cost the same or more than Medium, so check rather than assume.

Budget by task, then effort, then model.

At a fixed effort, cost varied 7.2–13.2× between tasks, effort moved it 1.5–9.0×, and the model 1.0–6.9×. Size the artefact first, then set the effort level, then pick the model.

Treat model choice as a per-task decision.

The cheapest model changed from cell to cell. Where a task will be repeated (weekly trackers, monthly decks), run it once on two models at Medium and lock in the cheaper one.

Plan for Fable 5.1 as a premium, metered model.

Fable 5.1 cost 0.6–6.9× the Auto/Opus 5 figure for the same cell and produced the most expensive run in the set. Reserve it for tasks where its output quality justifies the premium, and re-check its pricing while it is in preview.

Ask for linked citations when auditability matters.

Decks cited sources as plain text rather than hyperlinks. If reviewers need to follow the evidence, ask explicitly for a sources slide with links or a Word appendix; Word and Excel outputs linked their sources without being asked twice.

Finish the matrix before setting policy.

90 of 90 cells are complete and every cell is a single run. The remaining 0 tasks cover — the findings above may shift once they land.

09

Method, sources & caveats

Sources

  • Test log: Cowork-Universal-Test-Matrix.xlsx (sheet Comparison, 90 rows) — task, industry, department, prompt, output type, model, effort, skills & plugins, tools, cost in credits and USD. Every cost figure in this report is reproduced from that sheet.
  • Evidence: BojanBuhac/Cowork-Comparison-Analysis → evidence on GitHub — 90 generated files, named Task – Model – Effort – title, published publicly so every figure in this report can be checked against the artefact it came from. Office files link to the Microsoft Office web viewer (opens in the browser, no sign-in), a direct download, and the file's GitHub page; HTML dashboards are embedded live in the report and can be downloaded from GitHub.
  • Output measures (words, headings, tables, slides, notes, charts, sheets, rows, formulas, source links) were extracted from the files themselves; page and slide previews were rendered from the files for this report and may differ slightly from Office rendering.
  • Billing background: Manage Copilot Cowork for your organization (model responses, tool and skill calls, image generation and browser tasks count toward consumption) and Choose a model for Copilot Cowork.

Caveats

  • Interim. 90 of 90 cells are complete; 0 of 10 tasks have not been run. Findings are limited to the FS Account Plan, MFG Supply Risk and HLS Workforce tasks.
  • One run per cell. Cowork is not deterministic; repeat runs are needed to estimate variance before treating a difference as real.
  • Task and format are still partly confounded. Output types map to a small number of tasks each (DOCX: 3 task(s), XLSX: 3 task(s), PPTX: 3 task(s)), so format averages still carry the character of those particular tasks.
  • Fable 5.1 is a preview model; its availability and metering may change.
  • Cost unit. Credits and USD are reproduced as entered in the workbook ($0.01 per credit).
